questions.q: A recipe calls for 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. If a baker uses 9 cups of flour, how many cups of sugar are needed?
questions.answer: Set up a proportion: $\dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{9}{x}$. Cross-multiply: $3x=18$, so $x=6$ cups of sugar.

questions.q: On a map, 1 inch represents 25 miles. If two cities are 7 inches apart on the map, what is the actual distance between them?
questions.answer: $7\times25=175$ miles.

questions.q: A shirt originally priced at 40 dollars is on sale for 25 percent off. Find the sale price.
questions.answer: Discount amount: $40\times0.25=10$ dollars. Sale price: $40-10=30$ dollars.

questions.q: A population increased from 4000 to 4600. Find the percent increase.
questions.answer: Increase: $4600-4000=600$. Percent increase: $\dfrac{600}{4000}\times100\%=15\%$.

questions.q: A car travels at 60 miles per hour. How many miles does it travel in 45 minutes?
questions.answer: $45$ minutes $=0.75$ hours. Distance $=60\times0.75=45$ miles.

questions.q: A factory produces 480 units in an 8-hour shift. Find the production rate in units per minute.
questions.answer: $8$ hours $=480$ minutes. Rate $=\dfrac{480\text{ units}}{480\text{ minutes}}=1$ unit per minute.

sections.heading: Reading and interpreting scatterplots and tables

questions.q: A table shows study hours and test scores: (2,65), (4,75), (6,85), (8,95). Describe the relationship between study hours and test score, and predict the score for 5 hours of study.
questions.answer: The relationship is linear: each additional 2 hours of study increases the score by 10 points, giving a rate of 5 points per hour. Using the pattern, for 5 hours: starting from (4,75), add half of the 2-hour increment ($5$ points): $75+5=80$.

sections.heading: Measures of center: mean, median, and mode

questions.q: Find the mean, median, and mode of the data set: $4,7,7,9,12,15$.
questions.answer: Mean $=\dfrac{4+7+7+9+12+15}{6}=\dfrac{54}{6}=9$. Median (average of the two middle values, 7 and 9): $\dfrac{7+9}{2}=8$. Mode: $7$ (appears twice, more than any other value).

questions.q: A data set has mean 20 and 5 values. If four of the values are $15,18,22,25$, find the fifth value.
questions.answer: Sum of all 5 values $=20\times5=100$. Sum of the known 4 values $=15+18+22+25=80$. Fifth value $=100-80=20$.

sections.heading: Measures of spread and the effect of outliers

questions.q: Find the range and explain the effect on the mean if an outlier of $50$ is added to the data set $10,12,14,16,18$.
questions.answer: Original range: $18-10=8$. Original mean: $\dfrac{10+12+14+16+18}{5}=\dfrac{70}{5}=14$. Adding the outlier $50$: new mean $=\dfrac{70+50}{6}=\dfrac{120}{6}=20$. The outlier significantly increases the mean (from 14 to 20) and greatly increases the range (from 8 to 40), showing that the mean and range are both highly sensitive to outliers, unlike the median.

questions.q: A survey of 200 students found 120 prefer math and 80 prefer science. If a student is selected at random, find the probability the student prefers math.

A two-way table shows: 50 students play sports and pass an exam; 20 play sports and fail; 30 don't play sports and pass; 10 don't play sports and fail. Find the probability a randomly selected student plays sports, given the student passed the exam.
questions.answer: Total who passed: $50+30=80$. Of those, $50$ play sports. Conditional probability: $\dfrac{50}{80}=0.625$, or $62.5\%$.

sections.heading: Population, sample, and margin of error

questions.q: A poll of 500 randomly selected voters found that 55% support a proposal, with a margin of error of 4%. Interpret this result and state the range of plausible values for the true population percentage.
questions.answer: The margin of error means the true percentage of all voters (the population) who support the proposal is likely between $55\%-4\%=51\%$ and $55\%+4\%=59\%$, based on this sample of 500 voters. It reflects the uncertainty introduced by surveying only a sample rather than the entire population.

questions.q: A student's final grade is weighted: homework counts 20%, tests count 50%, and the final exam counts 30%. If the student scores 90 on homework, 80 on tests, and 85 on the final exam, find the weighted final grade.
A store mixes 3 pounds of coffee costing 8 dollars per pound with 2 pounds of coffee costing 13 dollars per pound. Find the price per pound of the mixture.
questions.answer: Total cost: $3(8)+2(13)=24+26=50$ dollars. Total weight: $3+2=5$ pounds. Price per pound: $\dfrac{50}{5}=10$ dollars.

questions.q: A machine produces 15 items per minute. Find the number of items produced in 3.5 hours.
questions.answer: Convert hours to minutes: $3.5\times60=210$ minutes. Total items: $15\times210=3150$ items.

questions.q: A car uses fuel at a rate of 28 miles per gallon. If gas costs 3.50 dollars per gallon, find the fuel cost for a 420-mile trip.
questions.answer: Gallons needed: $\dfrac{420}{28}=15$ gallons. Fuel cost: $15\times3.50=52.50$ dollars.

questions.q: A stock price increases by 20% one year, then decreases by 20% the next year. If the original price was 100 dollars, find the final price, and explain why it is not back to 100 dollars.
questions.answer: After the increase: $100(1.20)=120$ dollars. After the decrease: $120(0.80)=96$ dollars. The final price is not back to the original because the percent decrease is applied to a larger base (120) than the percent increase was applied to (100), so the dollar amount lost in the decrease ($24$) exceeds the dollar amount gained in the increase ($20$).

questions.q: A population density is 150 people per square mile. If a city has an area of 24 square miles, find the total population.
questions.answer: Population $=150\times24=3600$ people.

questions.q: Three workers can complete a job in 12 hours together. If they work at the same combined rate, how many hours would it take 2 workers with the same total capacity to complete a job that is 1.5 times as large?
questions.answer: Combined rate for 3 workers: $\dfrac{1\text{ job}}{12\text{ hours}}$. For 2 workers with proportionally less capacity (assuming equal individual rates), the rate scales down to $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the original: $\dfrac{2}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{12}=\dfrac{1}{18}$ jobs per hour. Time for 1.5 jobs: $1.5\div\dfrac{1}{18}=1.5\times18=27$ hours.
